gladius.description: The British Museum dates the Hod Hill comparison to the first century CE.

sources.title: British Museum · Sword from Hod Hill, 1892,0901.452

axe.description: The British Museum assigns this range to the Hurbuck woodworking tools.

sources.title: British Museum · Room 41 guide: Hurbuck woodworking tools

longsword.description: Fitzwilliam catalogues its hand-and-a-half sword within the thirteenth century; the model is a modern replica representation.

arming.description: The Met comparison is Western European, possibly Italian, about 1450.

sources.title: The Met · Sword, possibly Italian, ca. 1450, 14.25.1096

mace.description: The Walters comparison is an Italian steel mace dated about 1550.

sources.title: The Walters Art Museum · Mace, ca. 1550, 51.529

yatagan.description: The dated comparison is Balkan, probably Prizren; this does not date the model.

sources.title: The Met · Yatagan with Scabbard, dated 1802–3, 32.75.261a, b

guards.description: The date marks the formation of the Irish Guards, not the manufacture of this model’s original.

sources.title: National Army Museum · The Irish Guards

arabic.description: The AWM comparison has no manufacture date and was associated with First World War use.

sources.title: Australian War Memorial · Arabian Scimitar Sword, REL/10204

katana.description: Historical Japanese vocabulary is used for a fantasy design; no historical manufacture date is assigned.

sources.title: Worcester Art Museum · Parts for a katana sword, 2014.336.4
The Met · Blade and Mounting for a Sword (Katana), 36.25.1728a, b
